national_raw_news.title: 31 mins ago | National 92 Delhi Police denies permission for proposed protests at Jantar Mantar; Delhi Metro shuts entry &#...
national_raw_news.content: The Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed protest by the CJP at Jantar Mantar in the national capital today, citing previous violations of guidelines and public safety concerns. Addressing the media in New Delhi yesterday, Delhi Police Joint Commissioner Nupur Prasad said, applications seeking permission to hold protests or other programmes at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days in advance. Ms Prasad noted that the CJP had previously been granted permission to hold a protest at the venue but had failed to comply with the prescribed guidelines and the undertakings given by the party. The Joint Commissioner said the decision to deny permission was taken in view of the party’s previous failure to adhere to Delhi Police guidelines and its own undertakings, as well as the prevailing law-and-order situation, public safety concerns and traffic regulations in the New Delhi area. Ms Prasad further stated that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita are currently in force in the area, imposing necessary restrictions to maintain public safety and law and order. The Joint Commissioner warned that Delhi Police will take appropriate legal action against anyone found violating the law. Delhi Police said the proposed gathering was being planned without the requisite permission. It added that the Supreme Court had also emphasised the importance of complying with the applicable legal requirements governing public demonstrations. It also stressed that organisers must inform participants about the applicable legal requirements and the consequences of taking part in an unauthorised gathering. The police said the restrictions being implemented are temporary and precautionary, aimed at preventing overcrowding, maintaining public order and ensuring the safety of protesters, residents and commuters. It also said that people should be able to raise their concerns peacefully and that its responsibility is to create conditions in which they can do so safely while ensuring that the city continues to function normally. Meanwhile, security arrangements have been strengthened across the national capital. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has announced that entry and exit facilities at 45 metro stations will remain closed till 6 this evening for security reasons. The situation will be reviewed by security agencies, and further updates will be issued accordingly. The affected stations include Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Lok Kalyan Marg, Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Seva Teerth and Mandi House. Interchange facilities will remain available at the affected stations, except at New Delhi Metro Station. Namo Bharat train services between Sarai Kale Khan and New Ashok Nagar stations in Delhi will remain suspended till 10 PM tonight. During this period, services between Anand Vihar station in Delhi and Modipuram station in Uttar Pradesh will continue to operate as per schedule. Passengers have been advised to plan their journeys accordingly. DCP Railway B. Bharat Reddy has said special security arrangements involving have been made at railway stations to maintain law and order in Delhi in view of the proposed protest. He said 334 Government Railway Police personnel, including around 120 women personnel, had been deployed across Delhi’s seven major railway stations. A request has also been made for the deployment of Central Armed Police Forces companies at railway stations. Furthermore, Delhi Traffic Police has also issued an advisory announcing possible traffic diversions today in various parts of the National Capital, depending on the prevailing situation. The advisory states that traffic movement may be affected at several stretches, including the roundabout at Shankar Road-Vande Mataram ‘T’ Point towards New Delhi, Mataram Marg, Jhandewalan, Panchkuian Marg, Mandi House, Ashoka Road to Jantar Mantar Road, Windsor Palace and Tolstoy to Janpath Crossing. Commuters have been advised to plan their journeys in advance and avoid non-essential travel. Delhi Police has reiterated that the restrictions are intended to maintain public order and ensure public safety while allowing people to express their concerns peacefully within the framework of the law.

national_raw_news.title: All 10 candidates from Uttar Pradesh, including 8 from BJP & 2 from Samajwadi Party, elected unopposed to Rajya Sabha 2 hours ago 34
national_raw_news.content: All 10 candidates for the Rajya Sabha from Uttar Pradesh, including eight from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and two from the Samajwadi Party (SP), were declared elected unopposed yesterday. Returning Officer Ajit Verma, Special Secretary of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly, confirmed the unopposed election of all 10 candidates. The BJP candidates are Dharampal Singh, Prakash Pal, Shruti Gangwar, Vidya Sagar Sonkar, Priyanka Rawat, Radhakant Ojha, Gopi Krishna Pandey and Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan. The SP candidates are Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath congratulated the BJP candidates, expressing confidence that they will contribute to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat and the country’s development. The unopposed election was made possible after the Samajwadi Party decided not to field a third candidate for the 10th seat, paving the way for all 10 candidates to be elected without a contest. The biennial elections were necessitated due to the expiry of the terms of 10 Rajya Sabha members from Uttar Pradesh on 25th of November. Among the Rajya Sabha members retiring from the state are Union ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma, BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brijlal and Seema Dwivedi, Samajwadi Party leader Ram Gopal Yadav and BSP’s Ramji Gautam. The seat vacated by former Deputy Chief Minister Dinesh Sharma had also remained vacant following his resignation after being appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
